newsitem.title: GERMANY: German PC maker returns to black in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: German PC maker returns to black in first quarter.

text.p: German computer maker Peacock AG said on Monday productivity gains and new financing arrangements enabled it to generate first-quarter operating profit of 4.3 million marks ($2.6 million) on 1.4 billion marks in sales.
The company, which lost 20 million marks in the business year that ended September 30, also said it expected a "clearly positive result" in 1996/97.

Financial support from the state of North Rhine-Westphalia and Deutsche Bank AG had allowed Peacock to reduce liabilities by about 25 million marks, said management board member Heinrich Spatz in a statement.
Inventory was reduced by 40 million marks as well, he said.

Peacock, which assembles and also distributes Pcs, eliminated 90 jobs, bringing its payroll to 700, said Spatz, who joined the company from Siemens Nixdorf Informationssystems AG as part of a shake-up in November.
The company would continue to cut jobs through the remainder of the year, he said.
First quarter revenue was down from 1.6 billion marks in the year-ago period because the company narrowed its product line to cut costs.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.675 German Marks)
